metadata.title: A sharp three-point kernel bound and conditional proportions of zeta zeros
metadata.description:
Correction: the global proportions and the short-interval corollary assume the framework of Wang's preprint arXiv:2609.24167v1. On 6 October 2026 its author replaced that preprint on arXiv by a notice that a new method is needed to obtain a good improvement, so those proportions are conditional on an argument its author no longer offers and are not claimed. The sharp ratio theorem, R(alpha,beta) <= sqrt 2 with equality only at (0,1) and (1,0), and the kernel-level inequality are unaffected and remain claimed.

We prove that the auxiliary ratio in Wang's three-point kernel argument has sharp maximum sqrt(2), attained exactly at (0,1) and (1,0). Substitution into the source-pinned framework of arXiv:2609.24167v1 gives a lower proportion 0.6725007995946757558... of nontrivial zeta zeros that are simple and on the critical line, with a distinct-zero companion 0.8362503997973378779.... Directed rational intervals and an independent 120-decimal interval replay certify the numerical comparisons. The global transfer depends on a recent unreviewed preprint. The result is asymptotic and does not prove the Riemann hypothesis.
metadata.version_notes: Correction: the source framework arXiv:2609.24167v1 has been replaced by its author with a notice; the global and short-interval proportions are now stated as conditional and not claimed; the sharp ratio theorem is unaffected. Title changed accordingly.
